initiative.title: Settings, reference files and prompts in the viewer
initiative.summary: Show every setting, reference file and prompt in the UI, with agent-led setup helpers for anything missing.
initiative.next_action: Wait for TASK-0039 reader switch to merge, then build m1 (Setup page: Integrations and Settings).

claims.statement: The UI shows everything that can be configured and whether it is set.
Each missing setting has a helper that hands its setup to an agent via copy-to-agent or an Up next note; no in-app wizard.
The UI shows every reference file the viewer uses, starting with the repo list.
The UI shows the prompts the viewer has: issue review, daily plan, daily review, Up next sweep.
Settings live in config/viewer.json; tool files in config/ (not a library group, shown only on Setup); prompt overrides in config/prompts/<id>.md; reference/ is prose on its own library page.
Daily plan, daily review and Up next sweep prompts do not exist in the viewer today; they are AGENTS.md conventions and skills.
One Setup page with Integrations, Settings, Reference files and Prompts sections.
Scalar settings edit in place; arrays, objects and commands go through a helper or editor.
All prompts become workspace files; defaults stay in the viewer and only customized prompts are written to the workspace.
Integrations get a live probe on page open, with Recheck.
Helpers use the note popover; Enter saves an Up next note.
Daily plan drafts from Steps priority; daily review covers recap, stale and waiting, agent flags retro, and drafts tomorrow; Up next sweep works the queue in priority order.
Build waits for TASK-0039 layout to land.

shape.appetite: One page with four sections; medium, including a prompt registry refactor.
shape.problem: Settings, reference files and prompts are invisible to a new user.
shape.recommended_shape: Setup page with Integrations (live probes + note-popover helpers), Settings (scalar edit), Reference files, Prompts (registry with workspace overrides and routine launch buttons).
success_moves: Integrations and Settings first: no prompt-code coupling.
Probe commands are configurable so tests use fakes like fake-acli.js.
One prompt registry is both what the page shows and what buttons send.
Defaults stay in the viewer; overrides only when customized, so upgrades reach untouched prompts.
Prompt files hold instruction text with named slots; conditional facts stay in code.

first_proof.question: Can live probes report integration state quickly and hand setup to an agent?
first_proof.artifact: Integrations section with gh and acli probes against fixture fakes
first_proof.decision_rule: If probes exceed ~1s or prompt for sign-in, switch to presence-only states with an explicit Check button.
